states.name: bars
states.gap: The two title-bar controls are out of register: B's Library toggle occupies device rows 19–42 while its View button occupies 20–43, so the left control sits 0.5 CSS px high in a 32 px bar; A's pair share rows 20–43 exactly, both icons centred at 15.75 CSS.
states.gapTheirs: Stats numerals carry no weight step: "188" is 34 device px wide in A vs 39 in B at an identical 16 px digit height, and "words" 59 vs 65 — A sets number and label in the same weight and leans entirely on the grey step (#4A4A4A vs #8C8C8C) to make the count stronger than its label, so the figure doesn't resolve at a glance; B carries the same grey step plus a semibold numeral.
states.verdict: These two bars are the same bar — 32 px title, 26 px stats, a full-bleed 0.5 px #DFDFDF rule at y=874, the same #8C8C8C title, the same #4A4A4A/#8C8C8C count-and-label pair, the same 16 CSS gaps between stat groups, the stats row centred to a quarter pixel in both — so the choice comes down to two flaws, and only one of them costs a writer anything. B's half-pixel icon misregistration is a defect nobody drafting a chapter will ever see; A's flat numeral is one you meet every time you drop your eyes to the bottom of the window for a word count and have to read the strip instead of glancing at it. A stats bar has exactly one job — answer 'how many' without breaking the sentence — and A makes you parse a grey to do it. Neither shot proves the chrome recedes: both are the resting state, so the dimmed stats bar, the vanished title bar, the View menu and the Palette are all still unaudited claims.

states.gapTheirs: The title bar reads 'Untitled.md' for a document that has no file — it invents an extension and a filename that is not on disk; A correctly reads 'Untitled'. Naming the document is the only job that bar has, and B's is a lie. Second offence in the same frame: the 6-px caret is drawn at x626–631 while the placeholder's 's' starts at x623, so the caret bisects the first glyph.
states.verdict: These are the same two bars twice, so the argument is fought in the last two pixels, and B loses it. B tells me my unsaved document is called 'Untitled.md' — I would go looking for that file — and then puts the caret straight through the 's' of its own placeholder, which is the kind of thing you see once and cannot unsee. A's stats bar earns its 26 px: the values carry 52–58% of their ink at full #4A4A4A against B's 42–45%, so '0' and '< 1 min' read as numbers and 'words'/'read' stay furniture, where B's read as slightly darker text. A's cost is a page with literally nothing on it but a blue tick, which is a colder start than it needs to be — but a cold start beats a wrong filename.

states.name: view-menu
states.gap: At the view-menu state B renders no menu at all: a scan of the whole frame finds 444 saturated pixels (the caret alone) versus A's 13,247, no panel border, no shadow, no pressed state on the View button. The button itself is drawn at #C1C1C1 on a #F7F7F7 page — about 1.3:1 contrast, an affordance you have to already know is there — and pressing it yields nothing, so focus mode, typeface, dark mode, hide bars and the command palette are unreachable.
states.gapTheirs: A's menu has a ragged left edge: 'Dark Mode' and 'Statistics' set their labels at x=2538 (physical, 2x) because they reserve the checkmark gutter, while 'Hide Bars' and 'All Commands…' start at 2516/2519 — a visible ~12 logical px stagger inside one four-item group; the section head 'TYPEFACE' sits at 2515, a third indent. The right column drifts too: unselected shortcuts right-align at ~2827, but 'Ctrl+D' on the selected row ends at ~2833 because the blue band's inner padding is 8px against the row's 15px, so the one row a writer is looking at is the one out of column.
states.verdict: The two bars are effectively the same object — same 26px stats bar, same #DFDFDF hairline at the same row, same #4A4A4A numbers against lighter labels, same left-of-centre title drift — so the whole judgement falls on the one thing this shot exists to show, and B hasn't built it. A opens a real menu: three groups on hairlines, a TYPEFACE head, checkmarks that tell you Duo and Statistics are on, shortcuts on the right, and an 'All Commands… Ctrl+K' way out, plus a grey pill under the View button so you can see what you pressed. B gives you a #C1C1C1 hamburger that does nothing — the quietest possible chrome is not restraint when the writer can't get to focus mode. A's own menu is sloppy at the pixel — two of four items in the last group forget the checkmark gutter and jump 12px left — but sloppy alignment inside a working menu beats no menu.

states.name: palette
states.gap: No palette at all: A opens a 459×363 CSS px panel — 42 px search field, hairline divider, WRITE/TEXT/VIEW groups, 24 px rows with right-aligned Ctrl+D / Ctrl+T / Ctrl+0 hints — where B shows bare page. The command surface is simply not built.
states.gapTheirs: Title bar reads 'Untitled.md' where B's identical 13 px/#8C8C8C slot reads 'sample.md' for the same passage — same 32 px bar, but A's centre is a placeholder, so the one thing the bar exists to say it doesn't say; and A's own palette hard-clips its last row ('Dark or Light Appearance' / 'Ctrl+Alt+N') through the baseline at device y=960 with no scroll fade, no scrollbar, no half-row masking.
states.verdict: The bars are the same bars — same heights, same hairline, same greys, right down to the stat number sitting darker than its label — so neither wins on chrome craft. A wins because when you ask for a command something opens; in B the keystroke goes nowhere and you are left with a title bar, a word count, and no way to reach Focus Mode or the typeface without leaving the keyboard. A's palette is not well made: it ends mid-word at the panel's rounded edge, so you cannot tell whether VIEW holds one command or twenty, and the full-bleed #0A94D6 selection bar is the loudest ink on a screen whose next-darkest chrome is #575757. A half-finished palette still beats no palette.
